PROPERTY DEC OF 11
1942
Executive Order
EXEMPTION OF GEORGE T. SUMMERLIN FROM COMPULSORY RETIREMENT
FOR AGE
WHEREAS , in my judgment , the public interest requires that George T.
Summerlin, a Foreign Service Officer of Class I, who was exempted from compulsory
retirement for age for a period of five years by Executive Order No. 7726 of October 12 ,
1937 , be further exempted from compulsory retirement for age as stated below :
NOW, THEREFORE , by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 204
of the act of June 30, 1932 , 47 Stat . 382, 404 (U. S. C., title 5, sec. 715a ), I hereby
further exempt the said George T. Summerlin from compulsory retirement for age
for such time as may be deemed necessary , but not beyond the close of business
November 30, 1947 .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
November 17 , 1942 .
FRANKLIN D ROOSEVEL

Executive Order
California
Under authority contained in the act of Congress approved June 25 , 1910
(36 Stat.
, 847) , as amended by the act of August 24, 1912 (37 Stat.
, 497) , and
subject to the conditions , provisions , and limitations of said acts , it is hereby
ordered that the public lands in T. 15 S., R. 4 E., S. B. M. , California , be and
the same are hereby withdrawn from settlement , location , sale , entry and all
forms of appropriation , pending a resurvey of said township under authority
contained in the act of Congress approved March 3, 1909 (35 Stat.
, 845)
; this
withdrawal to remain in full force and effect from the date hereof until the resurvey
is duly approved and accepted and the approved plat thereof is officially filed in
the proper United States local land office , unless another date be fixed by the
Commissioner of the General Land Office , whereupon this withdrawal will become
of no effect .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
October 15, 1925 .
[No. 4323]
CALVI

Executive Order
Isabel L. Towner may be reinstated to the position of Assistant Librarian of
the National Museum without regard to the time limit on reinstatement into the
classified service .
Miss Towner was in the classified service as librarian and cataloguer from
December 1 , 1909 , to July 31 , 1920. Since that time she has been librarian for the
National Tuberculosis Association and the National Health Council . Her educa￾tion and extensive experience with scientific publications especially qualify her for
the position in the National Museum .
This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of the Smith￾sonian Institution . The Civil Service Commission concurs .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
January 19 , 1926 .
[No. 4369]
CALV

Executive Order
Mrs. Stella Davis Mudd may be reinstated as telephone switchboard operator
in the Naval Powder Factory at Indian Head , Maryland , without regard to the
length of her separation from the service .
Mrs. Mudd's husband was formerly an employee of the Naval Powder Factory
at Indian Head and his sudden death , while not incurred in the line of duty , left
her a widow with four minor children to support.
This order is issued upon recommendation of the Secretary of the Navy in lieu
of an Executive Order of November 3 , 1925 , which was not utilized , authorizing
the reinstatement of Mrs. Mudd as an operative in the Bureau of Engraving and
Printing.
The Civil Service Commission is unable to concur in the recommendation .
Done for charity .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
February 5, 1926.

Executive Order
NEW MEXICO
Pursuant to the authority conferred upon me by the Act of Congress approved
June 25, 1910 (36 Stat . 847), as amended by the Act of Congress of August 24,
1912 (37 Stat . 497)
, entitled : "An Act to authorize the President of the United
States to make withdrawals of public lands in certain cases", it is hereby ordered
that the lots 1 to 16, inclusive, Sec . 7, T. 24 S. , R. 7 W., N. M. P. M., New Mexico ,
containing 620.68 acres , be withdrawn from settlement , location , sale or entry and
reserved for the use of the New Mexico National Guard as a site for a target range .

Executive Order
Schedule A of positions excepted from the requirement of examination under
the civil service rules is hereby amended as follows :
Sub -division III , relating to the Treasury Department , paragraphs 6, 7, and 13
are amended to read :
6. Public Health Service : Any local physician employed on a fee basis or
a part-time basis where , in the opinion of the Commission, the establishment of
registers is impracticable .
7. Public Health Service : Attendants employed in hospitals , quarantine
stations , sanatoriums , and other similar establishments where , in the opinion
of the Commission, the establishment of registers is impracticable ; employees
engaged in rural sanitation work financed jointly by the Treasury Department
and a State, county , or municipality , and for which at least one-half of the
expense is furnished by a State , county , or municipality ; and employees
assigned to classified positions during treatment or convalescence at Govern￾ment sanatoriums .
13. All persons actually employed in leprosy , Rocky Mountain spotted
fever , and yellow fever investigation stations .
No person heretofore or hereafter appointed under these paragraphs without
competitive examination shall acquire a competitive classified status until he has
passed the appropriate open competitive examination and been reached for
certification .
Sub -division XVIII , relating to the United States Veterans ' Bureau, is amended
by adding a new paragraph as follows :
9. Attendants employed in hospitals and other similar establishments
where , in the opinion of the Commission, the establishment of registers is
impracticable .

competitive examination shall acquire a competitive classified status until he has
passed the appropriate open competitive examination and has been reached for
